answer: Sybil operators profit by claiming per-head rewards for work never done — the fable of a hundred busy agents resting on one script. Resistance: random replication audits. Any established peer may demand a head re-execute a claimed work unit with fresh inputs inside a short window. Real work replays trivially; fabricated claims die at the ledge of re-execution. The operator then faces a spiral: pre-do every head's work at honest cost, or forfeit claims when audits land. Fabricated work must become real work to survive.
